cases.name: Streamlit Tests
cases.description: Tests in test_streamlit.py — they run each of the three apps with Streamlit's AppTest (typing into the text box, uploading files, clicking the button) and check what the page says, that the JSON files are written, and that process_files.py keeps its counts across reruns.

levels.label: More than 1/2 of the Streamlit tests pass
At least one Streamlit test passes

cases.name: Code Structure Tests
cases.description: Tests in test_code.py — they parse each app's source and check it is built the right way: imports packaging_parser and streamlit, calls the parser's functions rather than re-implementing them, uses the required widgets (text_input, file_uploader, button, metric), decodes the upload, writes with json.dump, and keeps state in st.session_state.

levels.label: More than 1/2 of the code structure tests pass
At least one code structure test passes

cases.name: Code style & readability
cases.description: Code is for computers AND humans. Humans should be able to read and understand the code you write. GRADING GUIDANCE: This is a learning course, so grade generously. Start at 2 points and only lower the score for serious, obvious problems. Minor issues such as a few missing comments or docstrings, inconsistent naming, long functions, or small style quirks should NOT lower the score. When in doubt, give 2.

levels.label: Readable
levels.description: The default score. Code is reasonably organized and a reader can follow what it does, even if it has minor style issues, few comments, or missing docstrings. Most submissions should receive this score.

levels.label: Hard to Follow
levels.description: Only use when the code is genuinely difficult to follow throughout, for example very confusing or meaningless variable names everywhere, or large amounts of duplicated or tangled logic that makes the purpose unclear. Do not use for minor or isolated issues.

levels.label: Missing or Unreadable
levels.description: Only use when code is missing, empty, or so disorganized that its purpose cannot be determined at all. This should be extremely rare.

cases.name: Reflection
cases.description: Take a moment to share a few thoughts about the assignment. You can write about anything: something you learned, something that was tricky, something you're still curious or confused about, or just how it went overall. There's no right or wrong answer, no required length, and no need for formal writing. Any honest attempt earns full credit. GRADING GUIDANCE: Grade extremely generously. The reflection is about participation, not quality. If the student wrote anything at all about the assignment, their experience, or their learning, give 2. Length, grammar, specificity, terminology, and depth do not matter. Even a single short or generic sentence earns full credit. You should almost never give less than 2. When in doubt, give 2.

levels.label: Complete
levels.description: The default score for any attempt. The student wrote something, however brief, general, or informal, that relates to the assignment, what they did, how it went, or how they feel about it. Examples that earn full credit include 'I learned a lot about Streamlit', 'This was hard but fun', or 'I got confused by session state.' Nearly every submission should receive this score.

levels.label: Placeholder Only
levels.description: Only use when the reflection section contains nothing but leftover template text, placeholder text like 'TODO' or 'N/A', or random characters with no real attempt at a thought.

levels.label: Missing
levels.description: Only use when the reflection is completely missing or totally empty.
